simple: This page is about `LineForce`, a constraint that pushes or pulls along an imaginary line between two attachments. As the attachments move, the line moves too, so the force always points at the other attachment. It can act like a magnet, getting stronger as things get closer. It is useful for magnets, tractor beams, and things that attract or push away from each other.
analogy: It is like two magnets: the force always points straight from one to the other, and with the inverse square setting on, it gets much stronger as they get close.
keyPoints: `LineForce` applies force along the line between `Attachment0` and `Attachment1`.
The direction updates automatically as the attachments move.
The `Magnitude` property sets how strong the force is. Flipping it between positive and negative switches the force between the two directions along the line.
By default force is applied at each attachment's spot. `ApplyAtCenterOfMass` moves it to each part's center.
`InverseSquareLaw = true` makes the force grow quickly as the attachments get closer, like real magnets.
When using the inverse square law, set `MaxForce` so the force cannot become endless when the attachments touch.
By default only `Attachment0` is pushed. `ReactionForceEnabled` pushes both, in equal and opposite directions.

terms.constraint: An object that controls how parts move, like an invisible motor, rope, or hand pushing them. Mover constraints push or spin parts for you.
terms.assembly: A group of parts that are welded or joined together so physics moves them as one piece. A car body plus its welded seats is one assembly.
terms.attachment: A small invisible point you put inside a part. Constraints hook onto attachments, the same way a rope ties onto a hook.
terms.Attachment0 / Attachment1: The two attachment slots a constraint uses. Attachment0 is usually the one that gets pushed; Attachment1 is the other end or the reference point.
terms.magnitude: The size or strength of something. A `Magnitude` of 500 is twice as strong as 250.
terms.inverse square law: A rule where force depends on 1 divided by distance times distance. Halve the distance, and the force becomes 4 times stronger.
terms.center of mass: The balance point of a part. Pushing there moves it without making it spin.
terms.reactionary force: The matching push on the other part in the opposite direction, so both parts move toward (or away from) each other.
terms.MaxForce: A cap on how strong the force can get, so it does not grow out of control.

example.title: Make one part attract another like a magnet
example.place: Script in ServerScriptService (with two unanchored parts named MagnetA and MagnetB in Workspace)
example.code:
local partA = workspace:WaitForChild("MagnetA")
local partB = workspace:WaitForChild("MagnetB")

local attachA = Instance.new("Attachment")
attachA.Parent = partA
local attachB = Instance.new("Attachment")
attachB.Parent = partB

local magnet = Instance.new("LineForce")
magnet.Attachment0 = attachA
magnet.Attachment1 = attachB
magnet.Magnitude = 2000 -- if the parts push apart, change this to -2000
magnet.InverseSquareLaw = true
magnet.MaxForce = 5000 -- stop the force from growing forever when very close
magnet.ReactionForceEnabled = true -- pull both parts toward each other
magnet.Parent = partA
explain: We find two parts and give each one an attachment.
We create a `LineForce` and connect both attachments.
`Magnitude` sets the strength. Its sign picks the direction along the line, so if your parts fly apart instead of together, flip it to a negative number.
`InverseSquareLaw` makes the pull stronger as they get closer, and `MaxForce` keeps it from going too high.
`ReactionForceEnabled` means both parts get pulled, so they meet in the middle.

watchOut: With `InverseSquareLaw` on and no `MaxForce`, the force can become huge when the attachments line up. Always set `MaxForce`.
`LineForce` needs both attachments set. Without `Attachment1` there is no line to push along.
If only one part moves, that is the default. Turn on `ReactionForceEnabled` for both to move.
